KY-2026-HB140.s: The bill would require Kentucky’s Transportation Cabinet to check highway lane markings and other road paint 6 months after they are applied. If the check fails, the cabinet would have to fix or repaint them within 30 days. It would affect state road work on highways and other roads.
KY-2026-HB140.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB145.s: The bill would let certain statewide elected officials hire some staff outside the normal classified-service approval rules when needed to carry out policy. It would also let those officials raise the pay of some classified employees, by administrative order, up to the middle of the pay range for that job level.
KY-2026-HB145.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB220.s: Kentucky HB 220 became law. It changes how pension spiking is handled for some retirees in the state, county, and state police retirement systems, and it applies to people who retired on or after July 1, 2022. The Kentucky Public Pensions Authority would have to review affected benefits and make any needed payment changes.
KY-2026-HB220.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB298.s: The bill would change rules for KEES college scholarship awards for students from certain private, parochial, or church schools. It would set how an equal grade point average is figured using Advanced Placement exam scores, dual credit course grades, or both. It would also update related school and scholarship laws to match these changes.
KY-2026-HB298.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB311.s: This law requires railroad companies to clear or remove brush and other plants that block views at crossings with public roads or highways. If a railroad company does not do this after written notice, the Transportation Cabinet or a local government may remove the plants and seek repayment from the company. It affects railroad companies, state agencies, and local governments.
KY-2026-HB311.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB397.s: The bill would set rules for lower Ohio River trophy catfish permits, including making any current permit expire on May 31, 2027. After the act takes effect, those permits could not be transferred or reissued, and new ones could not be issued after that date. It would also bar most transport of live trophy catfish, except by boat while fishing, and make breaking that rule a misdemeanor for the first offense and a felony for later offenses.
KY-2026-HB397.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB407.s: The bill would change the rules for certificate of need applications, which are requests for state approval for certain health care projects. It would set who may ask for public hearings, who gets notice, who may speak or bring a lawyer at those hearings, and how reconsideration and appeals would work. It would also require the health cabinet to make a final decision within 90 days.
KY-2026-HB407.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB519.s: The bill would let people ask for a note on an instruction permit, driver’s license, or state ID showing they have a communication disorder, which means trouble with speaking, understanding, or using words. It would also let them ask to remove that note later, with no fee for adding or removing it. The Kentucky State Police would have to train staff on how to interact with people who have a communication disorder. It would take effect July 1, 2027.
KY-2026-HB519.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB535.s: The bill would change rules for investor-owned electric utilities and the state utility commission. It would set new terms for utility financing, including rules for securitized bonds, and would require a utility to seek in-state dispatchable power, meaning electric generation that can be turned on when needed, along with a 2-year freeze on base rates. It would also change how some storm, generation, and other costs can be handled, and it would let the commission approve sales or transfers of certain utility assets even if the costs are being repaid through securitized bonds.
KY-2026-HB535.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB558.s: The bill would make District Courts the only courts that can hear protective order petitions under Kentucky law. It would also make a related law match that change.
KY-2026-HB558.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB567.s: This bill would change Kentucky's open records rules for who counts as a resident of the state. It would let the official keeper of public records ask for a government photo ID with an address to prove residency before someone can inspect records, and it would allow another form of ID or proof if the person does not have photo ID. It would also update related rules to match these changes.
KY-2026-HB567.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB613.s: The bill would let certain fire protection districts and volunteer fire department districts raise their tax rate above the current cap if they hold a public hearing and notify the public. It also sets a way for the public to recall, or remove, the part of the tax increase above last year’s rate. The new rules would take effect on January 1, 2027.
KY-2026-HB613.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB658.s: The bill would require the Transportation Cabinet to adopt rules to extend how long a limited commercial driver's license can last, up to the maximum allowed under federal rules. It affects people who use a limited CDL. The measure is marked as an emergency.
KY-2026-HB658.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB687.s: The bill would let a county judge/executive hire someone to do certain duties when a stray horse or other equine is taken up by an animal sheltering group. The county fiscal court would have to approve the contract. It would also give immunity from criminal and civil liability for those duties.
KY-2026-HB687.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB727.s: The bill would let the Education Professional Standards Board use teacher certification fee money to build and keep up the Kentucky Educator Placement Service System, or KEPS. It would also require KEPS to let a person apply to more than one school district through the system. The bill became law and makes technical changes to state education rules.
KY-2026-HB727.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB755.s: The bill would let public employee labor groups represent only members who pay dues. Public employees who are not members could choose their own lawyer, if they follow reasonable employer rules, and could also make a written deal with the labor group for representation for a reasonable fee. It would also let the labor group represent a nonmember in a dispute over a collective bargaining agreement, which is a workplace agreement between labor and management.
KY-2026-HB755.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB826.s: The law requires at least 85% of general fund money for the Office of Adult Education to be used for adult education programs and goals. It also requires the test for a High School Equivalency Diploma to include a written or paper version. It affects adult education programs and people seeking that diploma.
KY-2026-HB826.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB869.s: The bill creates a rural building and job creation fund to help with certain tax credit program risks and to make low-interest loans for new buildings or renovations for lease to target wage projects. It also directs the economic development cabinet to report on the fund, work with a workforce liaison to promote jobs from incentive programs, and study reciprocity with other states on economic development programs. The bill also keeps one general fund appropriation from lapsing and treats the measure as an emergency law.
KY-2026-HB869.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB94.s: The bill would require Kentucky’s Council on Postsecondary Education to create and keep up statewide transfer paths for some bachelor’s degree programs at public colleges and universities. It would also require the council to post those paths on its website and would require schools in those paths to accept certain transfer credits as general education credit before treating them as elective credit. The council would also have to notify public colleges and help with credit transfer talks when a school plans changes that affect lower-level courses.
KY-2026-HB94.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HCR103.s: The resolution would create a Health Care Workforce Task Force to look for ways to increase the number of health care workers while keeping care standards high. It would set who serves on the task force and require a report with recommendations to be sent by December 1, 2026. The measure affects health care workers, schools, and state lawmakers who review the report.
KY-2026-HCR103.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HCR66.s: A legislative resolution would reestablish a task force to study how Kentucky prepares for, responds to, and recovers from natural disasters. The group would look at risk, stronger infrastructure, and planning, and would send its ideas to the Legislative Research Commission by December 1, 2026.
KY-2026-HCR66.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HJR81.s: This joint resolution would let the state budget director release part of the money already set aside for a water and wastewater aid program for troubled or low-income systems. It affects the Kentucky Water and Wastewater Assistance for Troubled or Economically Restrained Systems Program and the state agencies that manage those funds. It also declares an emergency, and it was signed by the governor as Acts Chapter 190.
KY-2026-HJR81.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HR136.s: The resolution recognizes April 28, 2026, as Pay It Forward Day in Kentucky. It is a formal statement from lawmakers honoring that day.
KY-2026-HR136.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB127.s: The bill would change how the cost of counting annual leave in a retiring teacher’s pension is paid in the Teachers' Retirement System. For leave earned through July 31, 2026, the state would pay the cost, and for leave earned on or after August 1, 2026, the worker’s last employer would pay it.
KY-2026-SB127.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB133.s: Changes reporting and audit rules for several local government bodies in Kentucky. Some entities could move from yearly audits to audits every 4 years after two clean audit reports, but they would go back to yearly audits if a later audit is not clean. It also combines some county clerk audit work into the regular audit, sets who pays part of that cost, and changes how final settlements are handled when a county official leaves office.
KY-2026-SB133.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB141.s: The bill would change Kentucky rules for legal ads in newspapers and digital newspapers. It would set which newspaper can be used, when other publication methods can be used, and the time window for publishing notices. It would also change ad rates and require some rules to be the same for public agencies and commercial customers.
KY-2026-SB141.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB147.s: The bill would set new steps for people to request vital records from state or county offices. It would raise the fee for a certified copy of a vital record to $10 and the fee for a certified copy of a birth record to $15, with some fee exceptions. It would also require the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to send the Annual Lifetime Kentucky Death Report to the State Board of Elections each year by July 1.
KY-2026-SB147.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB156.s: The bill would bar marriage for anyone under 18 in Kentucky and stop county clerks from issuing marriage licenses to people under 18. It would also end the court process that lets 17-year-olds ask permission to marry. Marriages already entered into in Kentucky before the bill takes effect, and marriages entered into in another state or country, would be treated differently under the bill.
KY-2026-SB156.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB160.s: The bill would set new rules for how Kentucky's health and family services cabinet handles child-care center license issues, including when it can require a correction plan, suspend a license, or revoke a license. It would also require weekly support contacts for centers with a first-time license and limit when violations can be issued during a probation period. The changes would apply to some pending cases and would take effect as an emergency measure.
KY-2026-SB160.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB197.s: The bill sets up a new county tier system for the Kentucky Business Investment Program, which helps approved companies get tax breaks and other incentives. Counties would be placed into four tax credit tiers each year based on unemployment and population data from the last five years. The level of aid for a project would depend on which county it is in. It was enacted as Chapter 202, with some line items vetoed.
KY-2026-SB197.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB214.s: The bill would let Kentucky’s Department of Agriculture accept money and grants from nonfederal sources, including public or private groups, if the funds support its programs. It also states an emergency, which means it would take effect right away. The bill was signed by the governor and became law.
KY-2026-SB214.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB261.s: Kentucky's fiscal courts would be allowed to help care for and maintain pedestrian swinging bridges used for public recreation. It would also give landowners some legal protection when they lease land to a local government that maintains one of these bridges on the property. The bill was signed by the Governor.
KY-2026-SB261.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB281.s: The bill would change how courts decide grandparent visitation cases in Kentucky. It would require clear and convincing evidence, which is a higher proof standard, and set factors a court may use to decide the child’s best interests. It would also update another child welfare law to match these changes.
KY-2026-SB281.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB312.s: The bill would let certified court security officers transport people who are being detained or are in custody when a court orders it. It would also let them go outside the court building area to do that transport and give them arrest powers while they are moving, watching, or guarding those people. It would also make changes so these officers can transport some people in mental health cases under set rules.
KY-2026-SB312.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB324.s: Kentucky SB 324 would change the state film tax credit rules. It would let unused parts of the $75 million credit cap carry into later years and raise the minimum spending needed to qualify. It would also expand the kinds of projects that can qualify to include video games, music videos, and commercials, and require a certified audit after production ends. The bill passed and was signed into law.
KY-2026-SB324.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB37.s: The bill would make the Treeing Walker Coonhound the official state dog of Kentucky. It passed and was signed by the governor.
KY-2026-SB37.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB56.s: This bill would change Kentucky Medicaid rules for nonopioid pain medicines. It would stop Medicaid from denying these drugs in favor of opioid pain medicines and from using stricter approval rules for them than for opioid or narcotic pain medicines.
KY-2026-SB56.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB66.s: Kentucky law now expands the list of drugs tied to impaired driving rules to include clonazepam, cyclobenzaprine, and fentanyl. It also requires people to be told that refusing a requested blood test can lead to a driver’s license suspension, and that a conviction under the law will also bring a suspension. The Transportation Cabinet must destroy records of moving traffic convictions that are more than 10 years old.
KY-2026-SB66.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB70.s: The bill would change who serves on Kentucky’s Public Pension Oversight Board and who can be appointed to it. It would add the chairs or vice chairs of two legislative committees and the State Treasurer, remove one governor appointee, and update the experience rules for some appointed members. It would also require the Kentucky Public Pensions Authority to report line-of-duty death benefit payments each year, along with line-of-duty disability payments.
KY-2026-SB70.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB8.s: The law changes how Kentucky’s Public Service Commission is set up and run. It sets who can serve as commissioners, how they are chosen and removed, and how long they may serve. It also changes some rules for utility cases, commission hiring and pay, and when the state needs approval to build certain electric transmission lines. It became law without the governor's signature and is an emergency act.
KY-2026-SB8.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB94.s: The bill would change Kentucky law on motor vehicle dealers by adding definitions for parts, repair orders, warranties, and warranty work. It would also set rules for how dealers handle warranty repairs, including time allowances, labor rates, parts markups, and payment steps. These changes would affect motor vehicle dealers and warranty repair work.
KY-2026-SB94.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SB98.s: Creates new rules for projects that use structural steel welding. It would require a certified welder and follow national welding standards, and it would not apply to welding done or asked for at a homeowner’s or farmer’s property. The law takes effect January 1, 2027.
KY-2026-SB98.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SCR66.s: A resolution asks the University of Kentucky and the University of Louisville to look into federal nuclear energy programs and to add classes and degree paths that train workers for new nuclear power plants. It also encourages the two schools to work with the U.S. Department of War on possible grants and research tied to nuclear energy. It became law on April 23, 2026.
KY-2026-SCR66.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SJR116.s: The resolution directs the University of Kentucky, the University of Louisville, and Eastern Kentucky University to work together on ways to help with doctor shortages and improve health care in underserved areas. It also calls for them to work with local groups, state agencies, and professional groups, and to send a report to the General Assembly by January 1, 2027. It passed and became law, with an effective date of July 1, 2026.
KY-2026-SJR116.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SJR54.s: This joint resolution would direct the Department for Libraries and Archives and the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to work together on ways to increase enrollment in Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library Program. It would also require them to report their progress to the Governor and the Legislative Research Commission by November 1, 2026.
KY-2026-SJR54.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SJR62.s: The resolution would direct Kentucky’s Division of Water to prepare a report with ideas for state and local governments on how to get easier access to public streams and waterways after flooding. The report would focus on cleanup and debris removal after floods. It would be due to the Legislative Research Commission by December 15, 2026.
KY-2026-SJR62.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SJR74.s: A joint resolution would direct the Legislative Research Commission and state agencies to work together on a statewide map of substance use disorder programs and funding sources. It would also require the commission to post the map on its website and send a report to the General Assembly by October 30, 2026.
KY-2026-SJR74.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SJR75.s: A joint resolution would direct the Public Service Commission to open one or more cases to look for ways to make utility service more affordable for people with low or fixed incomes. The commission would also have to report its findings to the Legislative Research Commission by September 1, 2027. It would declare an emergency.
KY-2026-SJR75.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR112.s: The resolution encourages the Legislative Research Commission to set up the Fatherhood and Family Engagement Task Force. It suggests what the task force should do and who should be on it. The task force would meet at least once a month during the 2026 interim and send a report by December 1, 2026.
KY-2026-SR112.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR144.s: The resolution would set March 31, 2026, as Kentucky Translational Science Day in the Commonwealth. It applies to the state as a whole. The Senate adopted it by voice vote.
KY-2026-SR144.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR161.s: The Senate adopted a resolution honoring Dave "Buzz" Baker for 37 years of service as the pre-game host for the UK Sports Network.
KY-2026-SR161.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR171.s: The resolution recognizes and honors Representative Al Gentry for his role in creating and helping golfer groups for people with disabilities. It is a formal statement of praise from the legislature. The resolution was adopted by voice vote.
KY-2026-SR171.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR204.s: This resolution would recommend placing a permanent statue of Mitch McConnell in the new State Capitol rotunda. It is a formal statement from the legislature about a public building display. The Senate adopted it by voice vote.
KY-2026-SR204.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR205.s: A Senate resolution would adjourn the Senate in honor and loving memory of Lorrie Anne Parker.
KY-2026-SR205.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR218.s: The resolution confirms Michael R. Eaves’s reappointment to the Eastern Kentucky University Board of Regents. His term would run until June 30, 2031.
KY-2026-SR218.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR221.s: The resolution would confirm Misdee Wrigley Miller’s appointment to the Kentucky Film Leadership Council. Her term would run through June 30, 2027.
KY-2026-SR221.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR224.s: This resolution confirms Soozie Eastman’s appointment to the Kentucky Film Leadership Council. Her term would run until June 30, 2029.
KY-2026-SR224.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR232.s: The resolution would confirm Angela Hatton’s reappointment to the Public Service Commission. Her term would run until July 1, 2029. The Senate adopted the resolution 38-0.
KY-2026-SR232.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR258.s: The resolution confirms Kenton W. Bottoms II’s appointment to the Fish and Wildlife Resources Commission. His term would end on December 31, 2028. It was adopted by the Senate.
KY-2026-SR258.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR272.s: Lawmakers adopted a resolution confirming Frank Penn’s appointment to the Kentucky Agricultural Finance Corporation. His term would expire on June 26, 2029.
KY-2026-SR272.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR294.s: The resolution would recognize May 8, 2026, as Provider Appreciation Day in Kentucky. It was adopted by voice vote in the Senate.
KY-2026-SR294.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR305.s: The Senate adopted a resolution censuring Kentucky Supreme Court Justice Kelly Thompson for remarks tied to pending impeachment proceedings. It would also direct a complaint to be filed with the Judicial Conduct Commission, the state panel that reviews judicial conduct, asking it to look at those remarks.
KY-2026-SR305.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR4.s: The Senate would adjourn in honor and loving memory of Minnesota State House Speaker Emerita Melissa Hortman. It is a formal statement of respect from the Senate.
KY-2026-SR4.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-SR98.s: A Senate resolution to adjourn in honor and loving memory of Paige "Nikki" Nicole Feltner. It was adopted by voice vote.
KY-2026-SR98.src: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)
